FACT_ID: sec05-R01 | anchor: A01
A wide leftward swing before a right turn can look like a lane change or left turn and prompt a following driver to pass on your right. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec05-R02 | anchor: A01
Swinging into a farther lane while completing a right turn can surprise drivers already in that lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec05-R03 | anchor: A02
During a left turn, avoid cutting across the corner into the path of a vehicle approaching from the left. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec05-R04 | anchor: A02
A left-turning driver must leave enough room for opposing traffic to turn left ahead of the vehicle. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec05-R05 | anchor: A02
When signs or lane markings allow multiple turning lanes, remain within your assigned lane through the turn. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0014]
